lessons: Build `open_tickets` the way `triage_pass` does: skip stems whose folded journal state is `merged`, and list only `tickets/<stem>/ticket.md` paths that are committed on main (reuse `_committed`-style check or `git.ls_files`). Never glob the working tree.

Add a test in tests/test_author.py whose first author reply names an already-committed stem. Assert the second author request's rendered prompt carries the stem-reuse finding, and that a valid second reply commits `chupa(<stem>): ticket`.

Add two criterion-4 tests that drive `main(["triage"])`: (a) a `bug_report` with no `has_repro`, (b) a pending message whose journal already has `author_invoked`. In each, assert a committed `decision-<id>` record, the message resolved as decision, and zero `author` requests.

Before declaring done, map every acceptance criterion (1-8) to a named test that asserts it. Criterion 3 needs both the stem-reuse and the validate_ticket re-prompt cases plus the exhaustion case. A 41-line test file cannot cover criteria 2-4.
Don't write `Outcome: ok` in run.md until every criterion has a test. The last run reported ok after about 15m of a 90m budget while three acceptance items were missing.
